WP_STEPS|/cleanW/overview: Clean tools thoroughly with water after use. Store in a cool and dry place: min. 12 months in the original container. Promptly use opened containers.
WP_STEPS|/cleanW/points/1: protect surfaces that are not to be treated
WP_STEPS|/planC/title: Assess the wall and the water
WP_STEPS|/planC/short: Where the concrete lets water through: joints, honeycombs, tie holes; WTA 4-6 — water pressure sets ≥ 3.0 mm dry film.
WP_STEPS|/planC/overview: Retroactive waterproofing from the inside in accordance with WTA datasheet 4-6: {RB400} and {AQ1K} withstand negative pressing water up to 0.75 bar. The material rate table of {RB400} for WTA 4-6: soil moisture and non-percolating water ≥ 2.0 mm dry film (≥ 2.4 kg/m²), water pressure ≥ 3.0 mm (≥ 3.6 kg/m²); transitions of concrete components without a tape ≥ 4.0 mm. Concrete lets water through where it is not dense — construction joints, honeycombing, tie holes — and along cracks.
WP_STEPS|/planC/points/0: {RB400} is flexible and crack-bridging (> 2 mm after PG MDS/FPD) and radon-tight — the choice for a concrete wall that may still move
WP_STEPS|/planC/points/1: moisture penetration from the rear must be kept off the flexible coating: pre-seal with {AQ1K} (RB400 data sheet)
WP_STEPS|/planC/points/2: water-bearing cracks are sealed first by injection — see the guide “Crack sealing / injection resins”
WP_STEPS|/planC/points/3: {AQ1K} in three application steps is the rigid alternative for substrates not prone to cracking
WP_STEPS|/prepC/short: Old paint, lime runs and laitance off by high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar); honeycombs broken out to sound concrete; matt damp.
WP_STEPS|/prepC/overview: A load-bearing substrate is the precondition for a lasting bond: less adhesive and bond-damaging substances — old coatings, lime leaching, laitance — are removed completely. High-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar, < 2000 bar) and jets with fixed blasting agents are suitable; the last step is cleaning with pressure water jetting. Honeycombed zones are broken out to sound, dense concrete; the substrate is even, pore open, sealed in the surface and matt damp at the time of application.
WP_STEPS|/prepC/points/0: requirement: load-bearing, even, pore open, sealed in the surface, free of adhesion inhibiting substances
WP_STEPS|/prepC/points/1: pre-moisten a dry substrate so that it is matt damp; the formation of puddles must be avoided
WP_STEPS|/prepC/points/2: in poorly ventilated rooms provide adequate ventilation
WP_STEPS|/repairC/title: Fill the defects, form the sealing cove
WP_STEPS|/repairC/short: Honeycombs, tie holes and the chased construction joint filled with ASOCRET-M30; cove of ASOCRET-M30 on an AQUAFIN-1K bonding slurry.
WP_STEPS|/repairC/overview: Depressions > 5 mm, mortar pockets, damaged areas and large-pored substrates are levelled in advance with {M30} (3–30 mm in one step). At the base slab–wall transition: pre-screen with {AQ1K} or {M30} in a consistency that is able to screen and, while still wet, install a sealing cove of {M30} with an edge height of at least 4 cm; after drying carry out the waterproofing.
WP_STEPS|/repairC/points/0: {M30}: watertight multi-mortar, water 4.5–5.25 l per 25 kg, pot life approx. 45 minutes, overcoat after approx. 3 hours
WP_STEPS|/repairC/points/1: edges are to be chamfered and corners rounded
WP_STEPS|/repairC/points/2: the construction joint: chased, cleaned and filled flush; the joint band of {RB400} follows over it
WP_STEPS|/presealC/short: One coat of AQUAFIN-1K brushed into the matt damp concrete — the rigid slurry keeps the moisture from the rear off the flexible coating.
WP_STEPS|/presealC/overview: Moisture penetration from the rear and intermittent moisture loading from the negative side must be kept off {RB400}; for waterproofing with moisture penetration from the rear, pre-sealing with {AQ1K} is recommended (RB400 data sheet). {AQ1K} is applied by brush into the matt damp substrate, up to 1 mm per step, approx. 1.75 kg/m² per mm; overcoat after approx. 6 hours.
WP_STEPS|/presealC/points/0: {AQ1K}: watertight against negative pressing water up to 0.75 bar (WTA 4-6)
WP_STEPS|/presealC/points/1: an application thickness of more than 2 kg/m² in one step can lead to cracking
WP_STEPS|/presealC/points/2: pot life approx. 60 minutes; clean tools with water
WP_STEPS|/jointC/short: AQUAFIN-RB400 at least 15 cm on both sides of the joint, two steps with the 6–8 mm notched trowel, smoothed: 4.0 mm dry film.
WP_STEPS|/jointC/overview: Transitions of watertight concrete building components with an immersion depth of up to 3 m (max. opening width 1.0 mm): apply the waterproofing to the prepared substrate to a minimum of 15 cm on both sides of the joint; processing in two application steps, total dry film thickness 4 mm; an even layer thickness is achieved using a 6 to 8 mm notched trowel and then smoothing. Alternatively the transition is sealed with the ASO-Dichtband system (then ≥ 2.5 mm).
WP_STEPS|/jointC/points/0: the joint band lies under the two full-area coats
WP_STEPS|/jointC/points/1: construction joints, horizontal and vertical, as well as intersections of waterproof and other concrete components
WP_STEPS|/coatC1/title: Apply the first coat of AQUAFIN-RB400
WP_STEPS|/coatC1/short: Trowel or brush over wall and floor strip, free of pores; even thickness with the coating-thickness trowel, then smoothing.
WP_STEPS|/coatC1/overview: Apply {RB400} in a minimum of two application steps ensuring it is free of pores. An even layer thickness is achieved using a coating thickness trowel or notched trowel and then smoothing. The material rate depends on the required dry film thickness (WTA 4-6: ≥ 3.0 mm for water pressure, ≥ 2.0 mm for soil moisture).
WP_STEPS|/coatC1/points/0: approx. 1.1 mm wet film per 1 mm dry film; approx. 1.2 kg/m² per mm dry
WP_STEPS|/coatC1/points/1: the second application step when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking — after approx. 3 hours
WP_STEPS|/coatC1/points/2: pot life approx. 45 minutes; do not add more water than max. 0.24 l per 24 kg
WP_STEPS|/coatC2/title: Apply the second coat to the class
WP_STEPS|/coatC2/short: When the first can no longer be damaged; spray or trowel, smoothed; ≥ 3.0 mm dry film in total for water pressure (WTA 4-6).
WP_STEPS|/coatC2/overview: The second (and following) application step takes place when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking. Water pressure from the negative side (WTA 4-6): ≥ 3.0 mm dry film, ≥ 3.6 kg/m²; soil moisture and non-percolating water: ≥ 2.0 mm, ≥ 2.4 kg/m². {RB400} can be sprayed; the fresh coat is smoothed with the flat trowel.
WP_STEPS|/coatC2/points/0: rainproof after approx. 3 hours, resistant to 1 bar pressurised water after approx. 16 hours
WP_STEPS|/coatC2/points/1: watertight against negative pressing water to 0.75 bar
WP_STEPS|/cureC/short: In dry rooms keep the coating damp for at least 3 days; ventilate deep pits for 24 hours; no condensation, no direct heating.
WP_STEPS|/cureC/overview: The material cures very well in areas with high humidity. In relatively dry areas, keep the coating damp for at least 3 days. In poorly ventilated rooms and deep pits, adequate ventilation should be provided for 24 hours; dropping below the dew point (condensation) on the surface is avoided with condensation dryers. Direct heating or uncontrolled blowing of warm air is not permitted.
WP_STEPS|/cureC/points/0: foot traffic after approx. 24 hours; withstands pressurised water after ≥ 1 day
WP_STEPS|/cureC/points/1: a plaster, tiles or a coating may follow on the cured waterproofing when the room is to be finished
WP_STEPS|/planT/short: DIN 18535: W1-B fill level ≤ 5 m, W2-B ≤ 10 m; crack width < 0.2 mm: 2.0 mm dry film; < 1.0 mm: 4.0 mm.
WP_STEPS|/planT/overview: The water exposure class of a container depends on the filling level: W1-B ≤ 5 m, W2-B ≤ 10 m, W3-B > 10 m. {RB400}: W2-B with crack width < 0.2 mm ≥ 2.0 mm dry film (≥ 2.4 kg/m²); crack width < 1.0 mm ≥ 4.0 mm (≥ 4.8 kg/m², special agreement necessary). {AQ2K} and {AQ1K}: tanks and pools > 2.0 mm, 3.5 kg/m².
WP_STEPS|/planT/points/0: {AQ1K}: W1-B, process and waste water tanks, repair of sulphate-damaged substrates; {AQ2K}: W1-B and W2-B, resistant to chlorinated water; {RB400}: W1-B and W2-B
WP_STEPS|/planT/points/1: in containers or with aggressive or soft water (hardness < 30 mg CaO per l) a water analysis is always required; the degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1
WP_STEPS|/planT/points/2: when used in swimming pool surrounds the pool water must comply with DIN 19643 ({AQ2K})
WP_STEPS|/planT/points/3: the specifications of the general building authority test certificates for MDS and FPD must be observed
WP_STEPS|/prepT/short: High-pressure water jetting; cracks repaired, voids levelled with ASOCRET-BIS-5/40 on ASOCRET-HS-FLEX, smoothed with ASOCRET-BIS-1/6.
WP_STEPS|/prepT/overview: System “Process water containers”: cracks are assessed and sealed; voids are levelled with {BIS540} (up to 40 mm in one application) on an {HSF} bonding coat wet in wet; the surface is smoothed with {BIS16} (max. 6 mm per layer) and finished with a felt or sponge board. Then the substrate is even, load-bearing, pore open and matt damp.
WP_STEPS|/prepT/points/0: high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar); the last step is cleaning with pressure water
WP_STEPS|/prepT/points/1: in the case of substrates damaged by de-icing salt, remove down to the neutral area (milling)
WP_STEPS|/prepT/points/2: water-bearing cracks are injected first — see the guide “Crack sealing / injection resins”
WP_STEPS|/prepT/points/3: the concrete restoration system is described in the guide “Concrete restoration”
WP_STEPS|/joint/title: Seal the wall–floor junction and the joints
WP_STEPS|/joint/short: AQUAFIN-RB400 at the junction, ASO-Dichtband-2000-S bonded without voids or folds, overcoated 15 cm on both sides.
WP_STEPS|/joint/overview: At wall–floor transitions and connecting joints, {RB400} is applied and the joint sealing tape ASO-Dichtband-2000-S is bonded without voids or folds. Transitions of watertight concrete components (immersion depth ≤ 3 m, opening ≤ 1.0 mm): waterproofing 15 cm on both sides of the joint in two steps to 4 mm dry film with a 6–8 mm notched trowel; or the bonded joint sealing tape overcoated at least 15 cm on both sides, minimum dry film thickness 2.5 mm.
WP_STEPS|/joint/points/0: alternatively a sealing cove of {M30} (edge height 4–6 cm) on a bonding slurry of {AQ1K} or {M30}
WP_STEPS|/joint/points/1: for movement and connecting joints use the ASO-Dichtband system components in accordance with their technical data sheets
WP_STEPS|/joint/points/2: floor drains and intersections must be provided with suitable flange elements
WP_STEPS|/coatT1/short: Spray, brush or trowel over walls and floor, free of pores; an even thickness with the coating-thickness trowel.
WP_STEPS|/coatT1/overview: Apply the waterproofing in a minimum of two application steps ensuring it is free of pores. An even layer thickness is achieved using a coating thickness trowel or notched trowel and then smoothing. System “Process water containers”: minimum two coats of {RB400} by spray, brush or trowel across all surfaces.
WP_STEPS|/coatT1/points/0: {RB400}: mix ratio 1.5 : 1, mixing 3 minutes, maturing 5 minutes, pot life approx. 45 minutes
WP_STEPS|/coatT1/points/1: {AQ2K}: mix ratio 2.5 : 1, pot life approx. 60 minutes, max. 1 mm per step
WP_STEPS|/coatT1/points/2: {AQ1K}: approx. 6.7 l water per 25 kg, pot life approx. 60 minutes, max. 1 mm per step
WP_STEPS|/coatT2/short: When the first coat can no longer be damaged: RB400 after approx. 3 h, 2K/M-PLUS 3–6 h, 1K 6 h.
WP_STEPS|/coatT2/overview: The second application step can be carried out when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking: {RB400} after approx. 3 hours, {AQ2K} after approx. 3–6 hours, {AQ1K} after approx. 6 hours. The total dry film thickness follows from the container class and the crack width.
WP_STEPS|/coatT2/points/0: an application thickness of more than 2 kg/m² in one step can lead to cracking ({AQ1K}, {AQ2K})
WP_STEPS|/coatT2/points/1: the waterproofing as a surface coating must not be exposed to point or linear loads
WP_STEPS|/cureT/short: Keep damp; avoid condensation with dryers; pressurised water after ≥ 1 day (RB400) or ≥ 7 days (1K, 2K/M-PLUS).
WP_STEPS|/cureT/overview: In service water tanks temperatures around +10 to +15 °C are usually expected: to ensure complete hydration of the cement the coating is kept damp for a sufficiently long period (constant relative humidity > 80 %) and protected against drying — 7 days are generally sufficient ({AQ1K}). {RB400} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 1 day (1 bar after approx. 16 hours), {AQ1K} and {AQ2K} after ≥ 7 days.
WP_STEPS|/cureT/points/0: dropping below the dew point (condensation) on the surface must be avoided with condensation dryers; direct heating or uncontrolled blowing warm air is not permitted
WP_STEPS|/cureT/points/1: the waterproofing must not be affected by water during binding
WP_STEPS|/cureT/points/2: {RB400}: in relatively dry areas keep the coating damp for at least 3 days; ventilate poorly ventilated rooms for 24 hours
WP_STEPS|/fill/short: After curing; with aggressive or soft water a water analysis is required.
WP_STEPS|/fill/overview: The container is filled after the waiting times of the technical data sheet. If applied in containers or in case of water loading with aggressive or soft water featuring hardness < 30 mg CaO per l, a water analysis is always required; the degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1.
WP_STEPS|/fill/points/0: resistant to concrete-damaging water in accordance with DIN 4030 (XA2)
WP_STEPS|/fill/points/1: {AQ2K}: resistant to contact with chlorinated water; pool water in accordance with DIN 19643
WP_STEPS|/planB/short: DIN 18534 W0-I to W3-I and DIN 18531: > 2.0 mm dry film, approx. 3.5 kg/m² plus 25 % allowance.
WP_STEPS|/planB/overview: {AQ2K} as bonded waterproofing with tiles and boards for water impact classes W0-I to W3-I (DIN 18534) and for balconies, loggias, arcades (DIN 18531) and terraces: dry film thickness > 2.0 mm, wet film approx. 2.2 mm, consumption 3.5 kg/m². Possible additional consumption on uneven substrates must be considered: a thickness allowance of at least 25 % in accordance with DIN 18531, 18534, 18535.
WP_STEPS|/planB/points/0: W3-I: surfaces around swimming pool perimeters, showers in sports facilities, industrial kitchens and laundries
WP_STEPS|/planB/points/1: system components after AbP AIV: joint sealing tapes ASO-Dichtband-2000, -2000-S, corners, sleeves ASO-Dichtmanschette-Boden/-Wand; tile adhesives AK7P, ASODUR-EKF, CRISTALLIT-FLEX, LIGHTFLEX, MONOFLEX (-fast, -FB, -white, -XL), SOLOFLEX, UNIFIX-S3 (-fast)
WP_STEPS|/prepB/short: Even, load-bearing, fully grouted; highly absorbent substrates primed with ASO-Unigrund; depressions levelled; matt damp.
WP_STEPS|/prepB/overview: Requirement for the substrate: even, free of adhesion inhibiting substances, sealed in the surface, pore open, load-bearing, extensively fully grouted. Highly absorbent and slightly sanding substrates must be primed with ASO-Unigrund-GE, -K, -S or -PLUS; the primer must have reacted fully before the subsequent work steps. Pre-moisten the dry substrate so that it is matt damp at the time of application.
